claims.text: A two-stage thermal decomposition of TiH2 or ZrH2 under high-pressure extrusion will suppress oxygen uptake.
A hydrogen-rich atmosphere during hydride decomposition will prevent nucleation of brittle alpha-HCP oxygen-associated phases.
The proposed processing route will produce a dense, single-phase BCC refractory high-entropy alloy.
The proposed processing route will maximize high-temperature yield strength.
The initial green body has an oxygen content of 500–1000 ppm.
The process requires 2 GPa uniaxial pressure during hot extrusion.
The process requires a vacuum below 10^-4 Pa together with controlled hydrogen partial pressure.
The specified thermal history is 50°C/min to 600°C, a 2-hour hold at 600°C, 10°C/min to 850°C, and a 4-hour hold at 850°C under 2 GPa.
A hydrogen backfill of 10^-2 Pa will maintain a reducing potential during processing.
Hydrogen generated in situ by hydride decomposition scavenges oxygen from powder surfaces.
High pressure suppresses void formation and promotes solid-state diffusion.
Rapid heating to 600°C triggers exothermic decomposition of the hydride precursors and releases hydrogen.
Released hydrogen kinetically inhibits diffusion of oxygen into the metal lattice.
Extrusion at 850°C facilitates densification and dynamic recrystallization of the BCC phase before brittle alpha-HCP phases nucleate.
The process traps the alloy in a metastable, oxygen-poor solid solution.
The resulting bulk material will exceed 99% of theoretical density.
The resulting material will have a ductile-to-brittle transition temperature below room temperature.
The resulting material will have a yield strength above 300 MPa at 1000°C.
The method fails when initial oxygen exceeds 2000 ppm.
The method fails above an extrusion temperature of 1100°C because oxide stability increases significantly.

contradictions.description: The environment is specified as below 10^-4 Pa while the simultaneous hydrogen backfill is specified as 10^-2 Pa. A 10^-2 Pa hydrogen partial pressure is incompatible with a total operating pressure below 10^-4 Pa unless the latter is intended only as the pre-backfill base pressure.

The predicted outcome only requires a transition temperature below room temperature, whereas the falsification rule rejects any value above -50°C. Values between -50°C and room temperature would therefore both satisfy the stated prediction and falsify the hypothesis.

The detrimental phase is alternately described as an 'alpha-HCP oxide,' an alpha-HCP phase nucleated by oxygen, and simply an alpha-HCP precipitate. These descriptions do not establish whether the target is a metallic oxygen-stabilized HCP phase or an oxide phase.
